steps: Greet the customer and confirm they wish to open a new bank account.
Ask the customer to provide their full legal name for verification.
Verify the customer's identity by requesting a government-issued photo ID.
Record the customer's full name as 'mary' in the system.
Ask the customer for their current residential address.
If address is not provided, note it as missing and proceed with caution.
Request the customer's date of birth for compliance and KYC purposes.
If birthday is not provided, flag for follow-up and proceed with alternative verification.
Ask the customer to present a valid government-issued document (e.g., passport, driver’s license).
If document is not provided, inform the customer it is required to proceed.
Confirm the type of account the customer wishes to open (e.g., checking, savings).
Explain the features, fees, and interest rates associated with the selected account type.
Ask if the customer would like to make an initial deposit.
If no initial deposit is provided, note that the account can still be opened with $0.
Confirm the preferred currency for the account (e.g., USD, EUR).
If currency is not specified, default to the local currency of the branch.
Enter all collected data into the bank’s core banking system.
Run automated compliance checks (e.g., AML, sanctions list screening).
Generate and present the account agreement for the customer to review and sign electronically or on paper.
Issue account details (account number, debit card if requested) and provide welcome materials.
